title: THE CHILD WHO OWNED THE EMERGENCY CHANNEL
deck: Fourteen-year-old Emi Sar has seized the only emergency radio in Kesh Province to keep rescuers moving toward the mine where her mother and thirty others are trapped, and her carrier is silencing the fire orders for six villages. Illuminara has fifty minutes before the east road burns and ninety before the mine runs out of air; to save both groups, she must let a child and an orchard keeper change the plan instead of asking them to trust another finished promise.
shape: Five scenes move from the relay hut, where Illuminara learns that Emi is guarding a list rather than a signal, through a fire truck where live road closures make the shared channel indispensable, into a protocol Emi repairs before releasing the carrier. Her manifest changes the mine rescue to two cage runs with extra air, while Mara Venn's Dunmere checkpoints make the evacuation audible. The aftermath leaves the mine closed, one orchard lost and Emi answerable, but every affected group keeps a voice, a record and a practical next step.

scenes.title: The Relay Hut
paragraphs: *Kesh Ridge relay hut · 14:02, fifty minutes before the east road burns*

The repeater hummed on the bench like a trapped wasp. Emi Sar sat in front of it with her mother's old headset over one ear and her thumb on a brass key worn smooth by thirty years of other people's emergencies. Outside, smoke leaned across the ridge in a long brown shoulder.

**Emi**  
Galen Doss. Present, pump bay. Tuvi Marek. Present, side drift. Ilse Orr—
A voice answered through static, thin and flat with distance.

**Sera**  
Ilse is here, baby. She is coughing but here.

**Emi**  
Ilse Orr, present. Thirty-one. I am keeping thirty-one.

Illuminara had landed fifty paces down the road and walked the rest. She stopped in the open doorway with both hands visible and the light she normally wore dimmed to a lamp's worth. She had heard the girl's carrier across half the province, a single unbroken tone that had flattened every other call on the net, and she had expected a hijacker. She found a child with a notebook open on her knee.

**Illuminara**  
I am Illuminara. I will not touch the equipment. I would like to listen before I ask for anything.

**Emi**  
Everybody listens first. Then somebody in a clean uniform asks me to stop.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will be the one who does not ask yet.

She stayed in the doorway. Every few minutes Emi read the names again, from the top, in exactly the same order, and a voice underground answered each. Illuminara watched the girl's pencil tick against the page after every reply. It was not panic. Panic did not keep a column.
*She is not guarding a signal. She is guarding a list.*

**Illuminara**  
Who is not on the mine's official roll?
Emi's pencil stopped.

**Emi**  
Fourteen of them. Mama brought them from the border camp last spring and the owner never filed their papers. If the mine says thirty-one people are down there, it has to say who. So there is no thirty-one. There is seventeen, and seventeen is what the rescue crews have been told to expect.

**Illuminara**  
And the reports?

**Emi**  
Three. The east gallery, the pump bay, the shaft collar. Mama wrote them in her own hand. Each came back stamped *resolved*.
She turned a page and showed it. Three carbon copies, each with a clean violet stamp over a crack someone had drawn in the margin.

**Emi**  
When I hold the channel, they keep saying her name. The moment I let go, she is a rumour again, and nobody sends a crew to a rumour.
Illuminara felt it land. She could have lifted the roof off the shaft in two breaths; the child had not asked for a roof. The child had asked to be counted.

**Illuminara**  
What would you need to hear, in order to let one second of it go?

**Emi**  
Not a promise.

**Illuminara**  
What, then?

**Emi**  
I would have to hear it happen, while it happens, on a line I can check.

scenes.title: What the Fire Truck Heard
paragraphs: *Orrel crossing, fire command truck · 14:19, thirty-three minutes before the east road burns*

The truck's cab smelled of wet ash and lukewarm coffee. Fire Chief Odo Brenn had a map of six villages taped to the dashboard and a handset that had not spoken to any of them in forty minutes. Beside him sat Captain Mirel Wynn of the provincial gendarmerie, helmet on her knee, a triangulation printout creased in her fist.

**Brenn**  
She is sitting on the only repeater that reaches Tamsin, Hale, Quill, Ansel, Dunmere and Orrel. The wind turned at noon. I have nine hundred people downwind and no way to tell them which road.

Smoke watch had filled two school buses at Hale, and five Dunmere orchard trucks waited at the lower gate. A patrol car could carry the first order to Hale in four minutes, but the fire was closing forks one by one; the latest sheet gave the east fork seven minutes. What the other villages needed was not one order but the next road while they were moving.

**Wynn**  
My team is eleven minutes from her door. I have orders to cut the transmitter.

**Illuminara**  
I have been in her door. I would like you to hear what the carrier is made of before you cut it.
She told them about the list. The fourteen unfiled names. The three stamped reports. Brenn's mouth thinned. Wynn did not move at all.

**Wynn**  
Which three?

**Illuminara**  
East gallery. Pump bay. Shaft collar.

**Wynn**  
The collar report came through my section. I forwarded it myself, six weeks ago. I was told it had been inspected and cleared.
The cab was quiet. Outside, a siren wound down without anyone touching it.

**Brenn**  
Captain, that does not make her carrier legal.

**Wynn**  
No. It makes it the only honest thing on that net.
Illuminara did not hurry them. She laid out what the girl could do and what she could not: Emi could not read a false assurance; she could read a name, answered live.

**Illuminara**  
Keep one line. Give each of you a window on it, out loud, in the open. Your orders first. The roll call last. Everybody hears both. Nobody has to believe anybody. They only have to check.

**Brenn**  
A car reaches Hale in four minutes. Why not send five more cars?

**Illuminara**  
Because the fork it reports burns in seven. A courier can start Hale; it cannot tell Dunmere's loaded trucks which turn is still open ten minutes later. Send the first car, and keep the repeater for the roads that change behind it.
Brenn looked at the seven-minute mark, then at five red arrows crossing five roads.

**Brenn**  
Fine. Thirty-eight seconds for fire orders. I can fit one route and one repeat if nobody decorates it.

**Wynn**  
South patrol to Hale. One car continues to Dunmere's lower gate. The team approaching Emi holds at Orrel.
Wynn did not pocket the folded printout. She kept it visible against her knee.

**Wynn**  
The girl keeps her key. My team holds with this report still in my hand. Record that I gave the order.

**Illuminara**  
She keeps her key. Momentary, not latched: she can cut in whenever a name is skipped or a window runs long. If she cuts in without cause, she answers for it later. If she has cause, you left her the means.

scenes.title: The Question No One Else Knew
paragraphs: *Kesh Ridge relay hut · 14:34, eighteen minutes before the east road burns*
Emi listened to the terms twice. Illuminara read them to her from a sheet Brenn's technician had typed on the truck's dashboard. She did not take her thumb off the key.

**Emi**  
You are all on the same side of the table, and I am the only one who has been lied to by every one of you.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Emi**  
That is it? Yes?

**Illuminara**  
You are correct about the stamps. I cannot make that untrue by being polite.
Emi's knuckles whitened on the brass.

**Emi**  
During his thirty-eight seconds, how do I know the mine is quiet because it is Brenn's turn and not because the roof fell?
Illuminara looked at the typed sheet. The neat division she had brought back from the truck had made silence look like obedience.

**Illuminara**  
You do not. I missed that.

**Emi**  
Then the mine gets the first two seconds of every minute. Someone says present. Brenn gets thirty-eight. The roll gets twenty. If present does not come, the fire window waits.

**Brenn**  
Agreed.

**Emi**  
And the key is not spent forever because one adult broke one window. It resets after every skipped name or proved overrun.

**Illuminara**  
Agreed. You found the hole. We change the protocol before you move your thumb.

**Emi**  
Then prove the thing I can check. You say you will go down. Anyone can say they go down. I will ask my mother a question that only she and I know, and she answers on the open line. Then you tell me which gallery you are standing in when she says it.

**Illuminara**  
Good. Ask it.
Emi pulled the headset tight. She spoke to the dark tone of the carrier as if it were a tunnel.

**Emi**  
Mama. The morning of the ninth. What did you leave on the stove?
For eleven seconds nothing came back but hiss. Then a laugh, cracked and wet, from deep underground.

**Sera**  
The good pot. The blue one. I left the lid off so you would be angry at me, not at the pot.
Emi shut her eyes. She did not cry. She wrote *blue pot* in the margin of the notebook, next to the first name, and her handwriting was steady.

**Illuminara**  
I am going down at the pump-bay shaft. I will say the gallery number every time I change levels. You will hear my voice move.

**Emi**  
And if you stop saying it?

**Illuminara**  
Then you have your key.
Emi eased her thumb off the brass. The carrier fell silent. For the first time in two hours, the net stayed open long enough for the new first check.

**Sera**  
Mine present.
Brenn's tired voice came in without ceremony.

**Brenn**  
Mine rescue, amend your roll: thirty-one below, not seventeen. Stage the second cage and more air. The first set runs short at fifteen-thirty-two for thirty-one.

**Mine-rescue lead**  
Second cage coming to the collar. Extra respirators with it. We search the side drift after the first lift.
Only then did Brenn give the road order.

**Brenn**  
All villages, this is Orrel command. East road closes at fourteen-fifty. Use the ridge track. Say again: ridge track.
Emi opened her mouth and closed it again. She had not expected the voice to sound so tired.

**Emi**  
He sounds scared.

**Illuminara**  
He is. So are you. He is saying it anyway.
Another voice entered before the minute closed, older than Emi's and roughened by smoke.

**Mara**  
Dunmere convoy. Five orchard trucks, forty-six people, lower gate. South patrol says the east fork is ash. We take mill lane. I am leaving the irrigation pumps.

**Brenn**  
Dunmere, mill lane is clear to the north culvert. Report when the fifth truck crosses.

**Mara**  
I will. Do not send anyone back for the trees.

scenes.title: Shaft Three
paragraphs: *Kesh cobalt mine, pump-bay shaft · 14:46, six minutes before the east road burns*

The shaft smelled of wet iron and burnt rubber. Illuminara went down fast, calling the level aloud at each landing: *level two, level three, east gallery*. Her voice, and no one's else, crackled in the girl's headset at the top of the hill.
At 14:47, before the rock closed around her, the shared line carried Mara again.

**Mara**  
Last Dunmere house clear. Fifth truck over the north culvert. The pump shed stays.

**Brenn**  
Logged. All Dunmere people clear.

At the sixth landing the rock stopped her. A slab the size of a barn door had come away from the gallery roof and settled across the passage on a crooked pair of timbers. Behind it, a lamp swung. Thirty-one tired people had made a small safe room in the place the owner had told them did not exist.

**Sera**  
We heard you count down the levels. Is that her? Is that my daughter's light?

**Illuminara**  
It is mine. Your daughter's is on the other end of the line, and she is keeping your names.

She set her shoulder under the slab and took its weight. It was not the kind of strength she would have chosen to show, but the timbers would not have held through another tremor, and the people behind them were not the ones who had to prove anything today.

**Illuminara**  
One at a time. Say your name when you pass. Emi is writing it down.
They came through low, with lamps, with scarves over their mouths. The first was a man whose hands had been bandaged with a shirt.

**Galen**  
Galen Doss.
Up on the ridge, Emi's pencil dropped a line through the first name. Down in the dust, Illuminara kept her voice level and the slab off their backs.

At the collar, the first cage rose with seventeen people and went down empty again. The second cage and the extra respirators arrived because Brenn had changed the roll to thirty-one. The mine-rescue lead sent two people into the side drift for the fourteen names the official sheet had omitted. Illuminara held the slab through both runs.
At 14:49, Brenn's window ran long. He was repeating a village's route, and the forty-sixth second of the minute passed with his voice still on the line.
The headset snapped. Emi's voice came through hard, her thumb on the key.

**Emi**  
Brenn. You are over.
Everyone on the net heard it. For six seconds nobody breathed. Then:

**Brenn**  
Understood. My window is yours. Ridge track. Out.
Emi let the cause-bound cut go early. When Brenn acknowledged the breach, the small reset lamp beside the key turned green again.

**Emi**  
Ilse Orr. Tuvi Marek. Present, present.
The roll call went on. The tally grew in her notebook, one pencil stroke at a time, and each stroke was a voice she could check.
At the last landing, a girl younger than Emi squinted into Illuminara's dimmed light as if it were a lamp from a story. Illuminara turned the glow up a degree so the child could see her own hands.
*Dust like snow, in the lamplight.* She had not expected to feel wonder in the shaft, under a slab, with a clock running. It came anyway, small and clean, and she let it.

**Sera**  
Thirty. One more behind me. Mine.
Sera Sar came through last, soot-blackened and gripping a hand-lamp she refused to put down. She did not say her name. Emi's voice said it for her, hoarse, over the channel.

**Emi**  
Sera Sar. Present.

**Sera**  
No, baby. Out.

scenes.title: The Tally at Zero
paragraphs: *Kesh Ridge relay hut · 15:41, forty-three minutes after the road burned*

The south patrol had reached Hale at 14:23; the open channel moved its buses at 14:35, sent Dunmere by mill lane at 14:36 and confirmed the fifth truck over the culvert at 14:47. By 14:52 the last Hale bus had turned before the fire crossed the east road at 14:58. Nine hundred people were on the high pastures. Dunmere had lost one orchard.
Emi still sat in front of the repeater. The carrier was silent, the channel crowded with ordinary voices: fire crews, a village midwife, a dispatcher reading out vehicle plates.

**Emi**  
Twenty-eight. Twenty-nine. Thirty. Thirty-one.
The last pencil stroke closed the column. She laid the pencil down.

**Illuminara**  
Zero missing. Zero names without an answer.

**Emi**  
Zero missing because they prepared for thirty-one, not seventeen.
Captain Wynn stood in the doorway with her cap in her hand and the folded printout still visible. She waited until the girl looked up.

**Wynn**  
I need your statement about the carrier and the reports. You will answer for the net. I will answer for my section.

**Emi**  
I know.

**Wynn**  
I will copy your three carbons here and read every stamp on this channel. You keep the originals.
Emi looked at her mother, who sat on an upturned crate with a blanket round her shoulders and a tin cup of tea going cold between both hands. Sera did not tell her what to do.

**Emi**  
I keep the key until the copying is done.

**Wynn**  
Agreed.
At 15:52 Wynn read the report numbers, stamps and dates into the handset, including the section that had forwarded one and been told it was resolved. Her own.

**Mara**  
Dunmere keeps its own household tally. Start with medicine, feed and wages. Three of mine rent their roofs, so their names are not on the property list. Titles come later.

**Wynn**  
The emergency account is open. Your copy governs the first payments.

The mine would not reopen. The fourteen unfiled workers would wait months for papers that should have existed a year ago. Emi would face a magistrate within the week. None of those costs was called a happy ending.
Illuminara stood at the hut door while the afternoon smoke thinned. Emi set the brass key on the bench beside the notebook, in plain view.

**Emi**  
Will you be there? At the inquiry?

**Illuminara**  
If you ask me.
Emi nodded, put the headset over one ear and found a clean page.

**Emi**  
Mara Venn.
Static breathed. Then:

**Mara**  
Present. Forty-six clear. One orchard gone. Start the next name.
Emi drew a line beside Mara's name.

critic_line: Illuminara, called to a burning province where a fourteen-year-old holds the only emergency radio so that her mother and thirty others stay counted, listens until she hears the hole in her own plan, and the child's thirty-one-name roll and resettable key make one shared channel that every office can check, so a second cage, extra air and live road orders bring all thirty-one miners and nine hundred villagers out, at the price of a closed mine, a lost orchard and a hearing Emi will face.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1; genuine independent GPT and Claude judgments; exact equal 50/50 arithmetic mean.
shared_strengths: Strong premise and humane, dialogue-heavy negotiation; the child's roll call, the verification question, and the protocol fix are moving. Weakened by dense logistics and timestamps, a compressed middle, and a tidy resolution that dilutes the tension.

A tense, lucid rescue plot turns procedural dialogue into humane drama: every rule change reveals character and makes accountability concrete. Emi's insistence on checkable action is memorable, and the ending preserves consequences. The prefatory synopsis slightly weakens suspense, while occasional schematic phrasing may feel over-engineered.
shared_reservations: Emi: "Mama. The morning of the ninth. What did you leave on the stove?" ... "The good pot. The blue one. I left the lid off so you would be angry at me, not at the pot."
When I hold the channel, they keep saying her name. The moment I let go, she is a rumour again, and nobody sends a crew to a rumour.

translation_sl.title: OTROK, KI JE IMEL V LASTI KANAL ZA NUJNE PRIMERE
translation_sl.deck: Štirinajstletna Emi Sar je zasedla edino radijsko zvezo za nujne primere v pokrajini Kesh, da bi reševalci še naprej hiteli proti rudniku, kjer so ujeti njena mati in še trideset ljudi, toda njen nosilni signal utišuje požarna navodila za šest vasi. Illuminara ima petdeset minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta, in devetdeset, preden v rudniku zmanjka zraka; da bi rešila obe skupini, mora otroku in varuhinji sadovnjaka dovoliti spremeniti načrt, namesto da ju prosi, naj zaupata še eni dokončani obljubi.
translation_sl.shape: Pet prizorov se premakne od relejne koče, kjer Illuminara spozna, da Emi varuje seznam, ne signala, prek gasilskega vozila, kjer sprotno zapiranje cest naredi skupni kanal nepogrešljiv, do protokola, ki ga Emi popravi, preden sprosti nosilni signal. Njen seznam spremeni reševanje v rudniku v dve vožnji kletke z dodatnim zrakom, medtem ko kontrolne točke Mare Venn v Dunmeru naredijo evakuacijo slišno. Posledice pustijo rudnik zaprt, en sadovnjak izgubljen in Emi odgovorno za dejanja, toda vsaka prizadeta skupina ohrani glas, zapis in praktičen naslednji korak.

scenes.title: Relejna koča
paragraphs: *Relejna koča na grebenu Kesh · 14:02, petdeset minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta*

Repetitor je na klopi brnel kakor ujeta osa. Emi Sar je sedela pred njim s starimi materinimi slušalkami čez eno uho in palcem na medeninastem ključu, ki so ga tri desetletja tujih nujnih primerov gladko obrabila. Zunaj se je dim čez greben nagibal kakor dolga rjava rama.

**Emi**  
Galen Doss. Prisoten, črpališče. Tuvi Marek. Prisoten, stranski rov. Ilse Orr—
Skozi statiko je odgovoril glas, tanek in sploščen od razdalje.

**Sera**  
Ilse je tukaj, dete. Kašlja, vendar je tukaj.

**Emi**  
Ilse Orr, prisotna. Enaintrideset. Ohranila bom vseh enaintrideset.

Illuminara je pristala petdeset korakov niže po cesti in preostanek prehodila. Ustavila se je v odprtih vratih z obema rokama na očeh in svetlobo, ki jo je navadno nosila, zatemnjeno na moč svetilke. Dekličin nosilni signal je slišala čez polovico pokrajine, en sam neprekinjen ton, ki je zadušil vsak drug klic po omrežju, zato je pričakovala ugrabiteljico. Našla je otroka z odprtim zvezkom na kolenih.

**Illuminara**  
Sem Illuminara. Opreme se ne bom dotaknila. Rada bi poslušala, preden kar koli prosim.

**Emi**  
Najprej vsi poslušajo. Potem me nekdo v čisti uniformi prosi, naj neham.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bom jaz tista, ki še ne bo prosila.

Ostala je med vrati. Vsakih nekaj minut je Emi znova prebrala imena, od začetka in natanko v enakem vrstnem redu, glas iz podzemlja pa je odgovoril na vsako. Illuminara je opazovala, kako je dekličin svinčnik po vsakem odgovoru potrkal ob stran. To ni bila panika. Panika ne vzdržuje stolpca.
*Ne varuje signala. Varuje seznam.*

**Illuminara**  
Koga ni na uradnem seznamu rudnika?
Emijin svinčnik je obstal.

**Emi**  
Štirinajst jih je. Mama jih je lansko pomlad pripeljala iz obmejnega taborišča, lastnik pa nikoli ni vložil njihovih dokumentov. Če rudnik reče, da je spodaj enaintrideset ljudi, mora povedati, kdo so. Zato enaintrideset ne obstaja. Obstaja sedemnajst, in reševalnim ekipam so rekli, naj pričakujejo sedemnajst.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj pa poročila?

**Emi**  
Tri. Vzhodni rov, črpališče, ustje jaška. Mama jih je napisala lastnoročno. Vsako se je vrnilo z žigom *rešeno*.
Obrnila je stran in ji jo pokazala. Tri kopije na indigo papirju, vsaka s čistim vijoličnim žigom čez razpoko, ki jo je nekdo narisal na rob.

**Emi**  
Ko držim kanal, ponavljajo njeno ime. V trenutku, ko ga spustim, spet postane govorica, ekipe pa nihče ne pošlje h govorici.
Illuminara je začutila težo teh besed. Streho jaška bi lahko dvignila v dveh vdihih; otrok ni prosil za streho. Otrok je prosil, naj ga preštejejo.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj bi morala slišati, da bi signal izpustila za eno sekundo?

**Emi**  
Ne obljube.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj pa?

**Emi**  
Morala bi slišati, da se zgodi, medtem ko se dogaja, na zvezi, ki jo lahko preverim.

scenes.title: Kar je slišalo gasilsko vozilo
paragraphs: *Križišče Orrel, gasilsko poveljniško vozilo · 14:19, triintrideset minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta*

Kabina vozila je dišala po mokrem pepelu in mlačni kavi. Gasilski poveljnik Odo Brenn je imel na armaturno ploščo prilepljen zemljevid šestih vasi in slušalko, ki se z nobeno od njih ni oglasila že štirideset minut. Ob njem je sedela stotnica pokrajinske žandarmerije Mirel Wynn, s čelado na kolenu in zmečkanim izpisom triangulacije v pesti.

**Brenn**  
Sedi na edinem repetitorju, ki doseže Tamsin, Hale, Quill, Ansel, Dunmere in Orrel. Veter se je opoldne obrnil. V smeri vetra imam devetsto ljudi, pa jim ne morem povedati, po kateri cesti naj gredo.

Požarna straža je v Halu napolnila dva šolska avtobusa, pri spodnjih vratih pa je čakalo pet sadjarskih tovornjakov iz Dunmera. Patruljni avtomobil bi lahko prvo navodilo v Hale odpeljal v štirih minutah, toda ogenj je zapiral odcepe enega za drugim; najnovejši list je vzhodnemu odcepu dajal sedem minut. Druge vasi niso potrebovale enega navodila, temveč naslednjo prosto cesto med premikanjem.

**Wynn**  
Moja ekipa je enajst minut od njenih vrat. Ukazano mi je prekiniti oddajnik.

**Illuminara**  
Bila sem v njenih vratih. Preden ga prekinete, bi rada, da slišite, iz česa je njen nosilni signal.
Povedala jima je o seznamu. O štirinajstih neprijavljenih imenih. O treh ožigosanih poročilih. Brenn je stisnil ustnice. Wynn se sploh ni premaknila.

**Wynn**  
Katera tri?

**Illuminara**  
Vzhodni rov. Črpališče. Ustje jaška.

**Wynn**  
Poročilo o ustju je šlo skozi moj oddelek. Pred šestimi tedni sem ga sama posredovala. Rekli so mi, da so ga pregledali in odobrili.
V kabini je zavladala tišina. Zunaj je sirena zamrla, ne da bi se je kdo dotaknil.

**Brenn**  
Stotnica, zaradi tega njen nosilni signal še ni zakonit.

**Wynn**  
Ne. Je pa zato edina poštena stvar na tem omrežju.
Illuminara ju ni priganjala. Pojasnila je, kaj deklica lahko stori in česa ne: Emi ne more prebrati lažnega zagotovila; lahko pa prebere ime, na katero nekdo v živo odgovori.

**Illuminara**  
Ohranite eno zvezo. Vsakemu dajte časovno okno, na glas in javno. Najprej vaša navodila. Nazadnje preverjanje imen. Vsi slišijo oboje. Nikomur ni treba nikomur verjeti. Samo preveriti morajo.

**Brenn**  
Avtomobil prispe v Hale v štirih minutah. Zakaj ne bi poslali še petih?

**Illuminara**  
Ker odcep, o katerem poroča, zgori v sedmih. Kurir lahko sproži Hale; deset minut pozneje pa naloženim tovornjakom iz Dunmera ne more povedati, kateri zavoj je še odprt. Pošljite prvi avtomobil in ohranite repetitor za ceste, ki se za njim spreminjajo.
Brenn je pogledal sedemminutno oznako, nato pet rdečih puščic, ki so prečkale pet cest.

**Brenn**  
Prav. Osemintrideset sekund za požarna navodila. Spravim noter eno pot in eno ponovitev, če nihče ne olepšuje.

**Wynn**  
Južna patrulja v Hale. En avtomobil nadaljuje do spodnjih vrat Dunmera. Ekipa, ki se približuje Emi, obstane v Orrelu.
Wynn prepognjenega izpisa ni spravila v žep. Obdržala ga je vidnega ob kolenu.

**Wynn**  
Deklica obdrži ključ. Moja ekipa počaka s tem poročilom še vedno v moji roki. Zabeležite, da sem jaz dala ukaz.

**Illuminara**  
Ključ obdrži. Trenuten, ne zaklenjen: kadar koli lahko prekine, če je ime preskočeno ali okno prekoračeno. Če prekine brez razloga, bo pozneje odgovarjala. Če razlog ima, ste ji pustili sredstvo.

scenes.title: Vprašanje, ki ga ni poznal nihče drug
paragraphs: *Relejna koča na grebenu Kesh · 14:34, osemnajst minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta*
Emi je pogoje poslušala dvakrat. Illuminara ji jih je prebrala z lista, ki ga je Brennov tehnik natipkal na armaturni plošči vozila. Palca ni umaknila s ključa.

**Emi**  
Vsi ste na isti strani mize, jaz pa sem edina, ki ji je vsak od vas lagal.

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Emi**  
To je vse? Da?

**Illuminara**  
Glede žigov imaš prav. S prijaznostjo tega ne morem narediti neresničnega.
Emijini členki so pobledeli na medenini.

**Emi**  
Kako med njegovimi osemintridesetimi sekundami vem, ali rudnik molči zato, ker je na vrsti Brenn, in ne zato, ker se je zrušila streha?
Illuminara je pogledala natipkani list. Urejena razdelitev, ki jo je prinesla iz vozila, je tišino prikazovala kot poslušnost.

**Illuminara**  
Ne veš. To sem spregledala.

**Emi**  
Potem rudnik dobi prvi dve sekundi vsake minute. Nekdo reče prisotni. Brenn dobi osemintrideset. Seznam dobi dvajset. Če odgovora ni, požarno okno počaka.

**Brenn**  
Dogovorjeno.

**Emi**  
In ključ ni za vedno porabljen zato, ker je ena odrasla oseba prekršila eno okno. Ponastavi se po vsakem preskočenem imenu ali dokazani prekoračitvi.

**Illuminara**  
Dogovorjeno. Našla si vrzel. Protokol spremenimo, preden premakneš palec.

**Emi**  
Potem dokaži stvar, ki jo lahko preverim. Praviš, da boš šla dol. Vsakdo lahko reče, da gre dol. Mamo bom vprašala nekaj, kar veva samo midve, in odgovorila bo po odprti zvezi. Potem mi poveš, v katerem rovu stojiš, ko to izgovori.

**Illuminara**  
Dobro. Vprašaj jo.
Emi je tesno pritisnila slušalke. Temnemu tonu nosilnega signala je govorila, kakor bi bil predor.

**Emi**  
Mama. Zjutraj devetega. Kaj si pustila na štedilniku?
Enajst sekund se ni vrnilo nič razen šuma. Nato se je globoko pod zemljo zaslišal smeh, hripav in moker.

**Sera**  
Dobri lonec. Modrega. Pokrov sem pustila odprt, da bi bila jezna name, ne na lonec.
Emi je zaprla oči. Ni jokala. Na rob zvezka ob prvo ime je zapisala *modri lonec* in njena pisava je bila mirna.

**Illuminara**  
Spustila se bom pri jašku ob črpališču. Ob vsaki menjavi ravni bom povedala številko rova. Slišala boš, kako se moj glas premika.

**Emi**  
In če jo nehaš govoriti?

**Illuminara**  
Potem imaš svoj ključ.
Emi je palec počasi umaknila z medenine. Nosilni signal je utihnil. Prvič v dveh urah je omrežje ostalo odprto dovolj dolgo za novo prvo preverjanje.

**Sera**  
Rudnik prisoten.
Brennov utrujeni glas se je oglasil brez slovesnosti.

**Brenn**  
Reševanje v rudniku, popravite seznam: spodaj je enaintrideset ljudi, ne sedemnajst. Pripravite drugo kletko in več zraka. Prva zaloga se bo ob petnajst dvaintrideset iztekla za enaintrideset ljudi.

**Vodja reševanja v rudniku**  
Druga kletka prihaja k ustju. Z njo dodatni dihalni aparati. Po prvem dvigu preiščemo stranski rov.
Šele nato je Brenn dal cestno navodilo.

**Brenn**  
Vse vasi, govori poveljstvo Orrel. Vzhodna cesta se zapre ob štirinajst petdeset. Uporabite grebensko pot. Ponavljam: grebenska pot.
Emi je odprla usta in jih spet zaprla. Ni pričakovala, da bo glas zvenel tako utrujeno.

**Emi**  
Sliši se prestrašen.

**Illuminara**  
Je. Tudi ti si. Vseeno to izgovarja.
Pred iztekom minute se je oglasil še en glas, starejši od Emijinega in raskav od dima.

**Mara**  
Konvoj Dunmere. Pet sadjarskih tovornjakov, šestinštirideset ljudi, spodnja vrata. Južna patrulja pravi, da je vzhodni odcep pepel. Gremo po mlinski poti. Zapuščam namakalne črpalke.

**Brenn**  
Dunmere, mlinska pot je prosta do severnega prepusta. Javite, ko prečka peti tovornjak.

**Mara**  
Bom. Nikogar ne pošiljajte nazaj po drevesa.

scenes.title: Jašek tri
paragraphs: *Kobaltnik Kesh, jašek pri črpališču · 14:46, šest minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta*

Jašek je smrdel po mokrem železu in zažgani gumi. Illuminara se je hitro spuščala in pri vsakem podestu na glas klicala raven: *druga raven, tretja raven, vzhodni rov*. Njen glas in noben drug je prasketal v dekličinih slušalkah na vrhu hriba.
Ob 14:47, preden jo je objela skala, je skupna zveza znova prenesla Marin glas.

**Mara**  
Zadnja hiša v Dunmeru je prazna. Peti tovornjak čez severni prepust. Črpališče ostaja.

**Brenn**  
Zabeleženo. Vsi prebivalci Dunmera na varnem.

Na šestem podestu jo je ustavila skala. Plošča v velikosti vrat skednja se je odtrgala od stropa rova in obležala čez poševni par tramov. Za njo se je zibala svetilka. Enaintrideset utrujenih ljudi si je uredilo majhen varen prostor tam, kjer je lastnik trdil, da ga ni.

**Sera**  
Slišali smo te odštevati ravni. Je to ona? Je to svetloba moje hčere?

**Illuminara**  
Moja je. Svetloba vaše hčere je na drugem koncu zveze in hrani vaša imena.

Z ramo se je podprla pod ploščo in prevzela njeno težo. Takšne moči ne bi želela pokazati, vendar tramovi še enega tresljaja ne bi zdržali, ljudje za njimi pa danes niso bili tisti, ki bi morali kar koli dokazovati.

**Illuminara**  
Eden po eden. Ko greste mimo, povejte svoje ime. Emi ga zapisuje.
Prihajali so sklonjeni, s svetilkami in rutami čez usta. Prvi je bil moški, čigar roke so bile obvezane s srajco.

**Galen**  
Galen Doss.
Na grebenu je Emijin svinčnik potegnil črto skozi prvo ime. Spodaj v prahu je Illuminara ohranjala miren glas in ploščo držala stran od njihovih hrbtov.

Ob ustju se je prva kletka dvignila s sedemnajstimi ljudmi in se prazna vrnila navzdol. Druga kletka in dodatni dihalni aparati so prispeli zato, ker je Brenn seznam popravil na enaintrideset. Vodja reševanja v rudniku je v stranski rov poslal dva človeka po štirinajst imen, ki jih je uradni list izpustil. Illuminara je ploščo držala med obema vožnjama.
Ob 14:49 je Brennovo okno trajalo predolgo. Ponavljal je pot neke vasi in šestinštirideseta sekunda minute je minila, ko je bil njegov glas še vedno na zvezi.
Slušalke so počile. Emijin glas se je oglasil trdo, njen palec na ključu.

**Emi**  
Brenn. Prekoračil si čas.
Vsi v omrežju so to slišali. Šest sekund ni nihče dihal. Nato:

**Brenn**  
Razumem. Moje okno je tvoje. Grebenska pot. Konec.
Emi je upravičeno prekinitev predčasno sprostila. Ko je Brenn priznal kršitev, je majhna lučka za ponastavitev ob ključu spet zasvetila zeleno.

**Emi**  
Ilse Orr. Tuvi Marek. Prisotna, prisoten.
Preverjanje imen se je nadaljevalo. Seštevek v njenem zvezku je rasel, po ena poteza svinčnika naenkrat, vsaka poteza pa je bila glas, ki ga je lahko preverila.
Na zadnjem podestu je deklica, mlajša od Emi, mežikala v Illuminarino pridušeno svetlobo, kakor bi bila svetilka iz zgodbe. Illuminara je sij okrepila za stopnjo, da je otrok lahko videl lastne roke.
*Prah kakor sneg v svetlobi svetilke.* Ni pričakovala, da bo občutila čudenje v jašku, pod ploščo, ko je čas tekel. Vseeno je prišlo, majhno in čisto, in dovolila si ga je.

**Sera**  
Trideset. Še eden za menoj. Moj.
Sera Sar je prišla zadnja, črna od saj in s svetilko v roki, ki je ni hotela odložiti. Ni izgovorila svojega imena. Emijin hripavi glas ga je izgovoril zanjo po kanalu.

**Emi**  
Sera Sar. Prisotna.

**Sera**  
Ne, dete. Zunaj.

scenes.title: Seštevek pri ničli
paragraphs: *Relejna koča na grebenu Kesh · 15:41, triinštirideset minut po požaru na cesti*

Južna patrulja je dosegla Hale ob 14:23; odprti kanal je njegove avtobuse premaknil ob 14:35, Dunmere usmeril po mlinski poti ob 14:36 in ob 14:47 potrdil peti tovornjak čez prepust. Do 14:52 je zadnji avtobus iz Hala zavil, preden je ogenj ob 14:58 prečkal vzhodno cesto. Devetsto ljudi je bilo na visokih pašnikih. Dunmere je izgubil en sadovnjak.
Emi je še vedno sedela pred repetitorjem. Nosilni signal je molčal, kanal pa je bil poln navadnih glasov: gasilskih ekip, vaške babice, dispečerja, ki je bral registrske tablice.

**Emi**  
Osemindvajset. Devetindvajset. Trideset. Enaintrideset.
Zadnja poteza svinčnika je zaprla stolpec. Svinčnik je odložila.

**Illuminara**  
Nič pogrešanih. Nobeno ime brez odgovora.

**Emi**  
Nič pogrešanih zato, ker so se pripravili na enaintrideset, ne na sedemnajst.
Stotnica Wynn je stala v vratih s kapo v roki in še vedno vidnim prepognjenim izpisom. Počakala je, da je deklica dvignila pogled.

**Wynn**  
Potrebujem tvojo izjavo o nosilnem signalu in poročilih. Ti boš odgovarjala za omrežje. Jaz bom odgovarjala za svoj oddelek.

**Emi**  
Vem.

**Wynn**  
Tukaj bom prekopirala tvoje tri kopije in po tem kanalu prebrala vsak žig. Izvirnike obdržiš.
Emi je pogledala svojo mater, ki je sedela na prevrnjenem zaboju z odejo okoli ramen in pločevinasto skodelico čaja, ki se je med njenima dlanema hladila. Sera ji ni povedala, kaj naj stori.

**Emi**  
Ključ obdržim, dokler kopiranje ni končano.

**Wynn**  
Dogovorjeno.
Ob 15:52 je Wynn v slušalko prebrala številke poročil, žige in datume, vključno z oddelkom, ki je enega posredoval in prejel obvestilo, da je zadeva rešena. Svojim.

**Mara**  
Dunmere vodi svoj seznam gospodinjstev. Začnite z zdravili, krmo in plačami. Trije moji najemajo streho, zato njihovih imen ni na seznamu lastnikov. Lastništvo pride pozneje.

**Wynn**  
Račun za nujne primere je odprt. Vaša kopija določa prva izplačila.

Rudnik se ne bo znova odprl. Štirinajst neprijavljenih delavcev bo mesece čakalo na dokumente, ki bi morali obstajati že pred letom. Emi bo v tednu dni stopila pred sodnika. Nobena od teh cen ni bila poimenovana srečen konec.
Illuminara je stala pri vratih koče, medtem ko se je popoldanski dim redčil. Emi je medeninasti ključ položila na klop ob zvezek, vsem na očeh.

**Emi**  
Boš tam? Na zaslišanju?

**Illuminara**  
Če me boš prosila.
Emi je pokimala, si namestila slušalke čez eno uho in poiskala čisto stran.

**Emi**  
Mara Venn.
Statika je zadihala. Nato:

**Mara**  
Prisotna. Šestinštirideset na varnem. En sadovnjak izgubljen. Začni naslednje ime.
Emi je ob Marinem imenu potegnila črto.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara, poklicana v gorečo pokrajino, kjer štirinajstletnica zaseda edino radijsko zvezo za nujne primere, da bi njena mati in še trideset ljudi ostali prešteti, posluša, dokler ne prepozna vrzeli v lastnem načrtu; otrokov seznam enaintridesetih imen in ključ, ki se ponastavi, ustvarita skupni kanal, ki ga lahko preveri vsak urad, zato druga kletka, dodatni zrak in sprotna cestna navodila rešijo vseh enaintrideset rudarjev in devetsto vaščanov, za ceno zaprtega rudnika, izgubljenega sadovnjaka in zaslišanja, ki čaka Emi.
